audit.intended_rules: Ch. 4 air travel: 14-day domestic advance-booking window (met, 20 days), economy mandatory on domestic (met), mandatory taxes/fees reimbursable (LuftVSt, passenger service, security). Ch. 9: flight tickets are not weekend expenses merely because a travel day falls on a weekend (Saturday return distractor). Ch. 3: total under €2,500, no pre-approval needed. Ch. 2: note states trip purpose as required for flights.
realism_issues: Base fare of €465 for a domestic BER-MUC economy round trip booked 20 days out is on the high side (typical €150-250), though no handbook cap exists
German LuftVSt of €54.20 exceeds the real 2024 domestic rate (~€13); the long-haul-rate-style figure is a plausible fake but not a handbook violation since taxes are reimbursed at face value
audit.notes: Validator passes; totals sum to the cent and charges mirror items. Correct adjudication: approved in full, €599.76. Case works as a valid-distribution example with built-in distractors (Saturday return date, itemized government taxes, moderately high fare) that all resolve to reimbursable. Lufthansa vendor identity, Frankfurt address, real-looking tax ID, and segment times are all consistent. No label.json or receipt.jpg to reconcile; consider adding a label.json if the case set requires labels for all cases.
